screening_rationale: Gulf coastal compound rainfall, river, and surge flooding; critical infrastructure exposure is well documented.
value_integration_question: Use as a high-hazard coastal baseline and test how observed-water overlap aligns with infrastructure and watershed planning.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: Houston’s FY2026–2030 CIP estimates $1.156 billion for storm-drainage improvements, with about $170 million for Local Drainage Program and Storm Water Action Team projects. The plan describes objective ranking of flood-protection needs and design for 2-year collection-system rainfall while reducing structural-flood risk during 100-year events.
value_dimensions: drainage service continuity; capital-project prioritization; neighborhood-level exposure
validation_path: Overlay only city-published drainage project and channel/detention geodata available for the 25 km study box; compare event-period satellite classifications with city/USGS gauge records and dated official flood reports. Record geometry/date coverage before analysis.
scope_limit: CIP allocations are planned estimates, not measured reductions in flood loss; the plan cautions that receiving-system capacity can still cause flooding.

screening_rationale: Coastal rainfall flooding interacts with groundwater table, high tides, and sea-level rise; NOAA-supported research targets prediction and risk management.
value_integration_question: Test a shallow-groundwater coastal setting and compare satellite water signals with documented local flood evidence.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: NOAA NCCOS reports a rainfall-flood model demonstrated over roughly 1,000 km² of Miami-Dade using rain, gauges, topography, land use, flood infrastructure, and groundwater. For a four-day May 2020 Memorial Day flood period, canal water levels were predicted with about 15 cm average accuracy and the model ran at least 30 times faster than real time.
value_dimensions: canal and drainage operations; groundwater-sensitive neighborhoods; equitable risk-management prioritization
validation_path: Use documented gauge/canal levels, rainfall timing, and independently mapped event reports for a held-out event; treat the NOAA 2020 experiment as contextual precedent, not as ATLAS ground truth or performance evidence.
scope_limit: The NOAA demonstration is county-scale and predates the current candidate window; it does not validate the 625 km² candidate box or ATLAS.

screening_rationale: USGS documented widespread Milton flooding in its Tampa coverage area, major-stage rivers, and field measurements/gage repairs.
value_integration_question: Test an event with independent hydrologic measurements and coastal/river flood context.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: USGS deployed eight wave sensors between Naples and Crystal River to measure Hurricane Milton coastal impacts and added a rapid deployment gauge in St. Petersburg; USGS also documented post-storm flood measurements and gauge repairs along Florida’s Gulf Coast.
value_dimensions: coastal water level; transport and utility access; recovery prioritization
validation_path: Match any candidate-box OPERA dates to USGS/NWS gauge time series and geolocated high-water marks or official event reports. Keep regional instruments outside the box as context and do not count them as local reference samples.
scope_limit: The cited sensors cover a regional coast and do not establish adequate independent labels inside the Tampa candidate box.

screening_rationale: Low elevation, levees, pumps, and a large catch-basin network create a documented urban rainfall-flood management problem.
value_integration_question: Test satellite screening in a pump-dependent, leveed urban drainage environment.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: municipal hazard plan and operating context
empirical_evidence: The City hazard-mitigation plan identifies six flood types and reports 24 city pump stations with total design capacity of 50,891 cfs. It also records 69 significant flooding events in 1997–2019 using NOAA Storm Events data, while warning that some NOAA damage fields are unreliable.
value_dimensions: pump-dependent drainage service; road and emergency access; low-lying community exposure
validation_path: Pre-register one dated event and baseline, then compare eligible OPERA pixels with city pump/drainage records, NWS rainfall and river stages, and dated official street-flood reports where spatial precision is sufficient.
scope_limit: The historical event count is not a geocoded independent truth set, and the City notes limitations in the NOAA records; pump design capacity is not actual operating capacity during any event.

screening_rationale: NOAA-hosted research maps present/future flood adaptation areas; infrastructure and power-system exposure are documented.
value_integration_question: Test dense coastal infrastructure and compare pluvial/coastal water exposure across an urban asset portfolio.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: NYC DEP’s December 2025 report identifies 86 priority drainage areas in its 2024 Stormwater Analysis and reports 325 FloodNet sensors plus 241 sewer monitors citywide. The monitoring supports flood tracking and sewer performance work; agency counts are not local to the candidate box.
value_dimensions: critical sewer and transport service; neighborhood drainage priorities; public sensor coverage
validation_path: Acquire dated FloodNet and NYC DEP records, independently review their spatial coverage against the 625 km² box, and validate a held-out event against municipal inundation or high-water labels rather than using capital-plan priority zones as truth.
scope_limit: The agency’s counts are citywide and do not imply that all sensors or priority areas fall within the candidate AOI.

screening_rationale: The City of Sacramento's 2024 flood-management plan documents riverine and stormwater hazards and describes the city's 2017 event response; the City's levee-break maps support scenario-planning relevance but are not observations.
value_integration_question: Test whether validated satellite water observations add timely spatial context to municipal incident records, river gauges, levee information, and public-infrastructure priorities.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: city flood-management planning and historical event context
empirical_evidence: The City of Sacramento's May 2024 Comprehensive Flood Management Plan describes riverine and localized stormwater risk and records its 2017 response, including flood impacts at Garcia Bend Park, I Street Bridge, NEMDC, and Magpie Creek. The City also publishes hypothetical levee-break maps for a 200-year flood scenario. The 2017 event is historical context outside the shared 2024–2026 observation window; the planning maps are modeled scenarios, not observed flood labels.
value_dimensions: levee-protected communities; transport and utility corridor exposure; risk communication
validation_path: For a held-out event inside the shared observation window, obtain dated City incident/closure records, Sacramento and American River gauge data, local levee records, and independent inundation extents. Geospatially verify each source against the frozen 25 km box, then apply the same three-scene-per-period, 80%-valid-pixel, probability-sampling, and dual-labeler protocol used for every other area.
scope_limit: The 2017 locations are city-reported historical context outside the shared 2024–2026 observation window and are not asserted to intersect the fixed box. The City's levee-break maps are hypothetical scenarios. Neither source provides reference pixels; Sacramento remains candidate-only until event-specific QA-valid observations and independent labels pass the common gate.

screening_rationale: The City’s 2025 comprehensive plan calls for stormwater management and flooding mitigation, including capital and watershed actions.
value_integration_question: Test an inland urban-runoff case and connect exposure evidence to watershed and public-infrastructure planning.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: municipal watershed planning and event response
empirical_evidence: Atlanta Watershed Management publishes ten watershed improvement plans that identify infrastructure needs and recommended projects. City emergency communications also document active monitoring of road, drainage, and public-safety conditions during heavy-rain flooding; this is direct management relevance but not a quantified citywide loss series.
value_dimensions: watershed and drainage investment; road access; neighborhood service equity
validation_path: Map plan project and stormwater geographies in the candidate box; evaluate a predeclared event using NWS rainfall, USGS stream gauges, and dated city incident/closure reports with location-level inclusion rules.
scope_limit: Plan coverage and agency response do not establish customer demand, parcel-level impacts, or independent event accuracy.

screening_rationale: NOAA/NWS river gauge documentation defines flood stages and describes levee/floodwall impacts along the Mississippi.
value_integration_question: Test a major-river and levee comparator with official river-stage context.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: NWS reports that the Mississippi River at St. Louis crested at 49.58 ft on August 1, 1993, then a record, during the region’s Great Flood. This provides a strong riverine/floodwall stress context for an inland comparator.
value_dimensions: river and floodwall exposure; regional transport continuity; long-term flood preparedness
validation_path: Use NOAA/NWS gauge records and recent dated event reports for actual validation; retain 1993 as contextual extreme-event history, not as a contemporaneous label for the 2024–2026 screen.
scope_limit: The headline evidence is historical and regional; it does not establish recent local flooding or current demand.

screening_rationale: Greater Jakarta faces regular widespread flooding alongside water-supply deficits and water-quality challenges; the World Bank calls for integrated urban water management.
value_integration_question: Study cross-jurisdictional water exposure and the integration of flood, water-supply, sanitation, and infrastructure planning.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: municipal flood-response capacity and multilateral research
empirical_evidence: DKI Jakarta reported 580 stationary pumps across 202 locations and 557 mobile pumps across its five administrative cities in 2024. The World Bank describes Greater Jakarta as a 14-municipality/district, three-province system facing recurring floods alongside water-supply and sanitation challenges, and calls for integrated urban-water management.
value_dimensions: pump and drainage operations; water quality and supply; cross-administration planning
validation_path: Obtain dated BPBD flood-event and pump-operation records, rainfall and river/gate levels, then spatially resolve them to the fixed AOI. Engage local technical partners to review translation, data licensing, and location bias.
scope_limit: Pump counts are response-capacity inventory, not utilization or measured effectiveness; Greater Jakarta evidence spans well beyond the selected box.

screening_rationale: PUB documents flash/coastal flood risks, investments in drainage, a national flood-resilience program, and extensive sensor monitoring.
value_integration_question: Test a data-rich, highly urbanized setting where satellite screening can be compared with agency sensors and flood reports.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: national drainage performance, current risk context, and exploratory event lead
empirical_evidence: PUB reports that flood-prone area fell from about 3,200 ha in the 1970s to less than 25 ha, a 99% reduction. Its current public page links a November 2025 list of 36 flood-prone locations and a 19-location hotspot list dated 2 February 2026. Separately, the data.gov.sg PUB Flood Alerts API returned an alert dated 2025-05-22 describing an observed flash flood at Wan Tho Ave (Pheng Geck Ave); the reported center falls inside the fixed Singapore AOI. The single point alert is an exploratory event lead, not a mapped flood extent, independent pixel label, or ATLAS result.
value_dimensions: drainage-service performance; urban transport and facility access; residual-risk hotspot prioritization
validation_path: For a held-out event, obtain dated PUB flood alerts, water-level sensor or rainfall records, and geospatial versions of the official hotspot/location lists. The published lists are named-location context, not event extents, and the alert supplies no event-specific extent geometry. Geocode and verify licensing before event intersection with the frozen common box; source an independent mapped extent or field reference and sample pixels under the common protocol before confirmatory testing.
scope_limit: The national area trend and citywide named-location lists cannot be attributed to the 625 km² screen without spatial validation. The 2025-05-22 alert is a single location lead, not a mapped flood extent, not an independent event label, and does not establish event frequency. Singapore remains candidate-only.

screening_rationale: Dubai Municipality’s AED 30bn Tasreef program expands stormwater collection and drainage; contracts cover critical urban areas.
value_integration_question: Test rapid urban growth and major drainage investment, while treating dry-climate extreme rainfall as an event-based case.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: Dubai Municipality reports AED 1.439 billion in contracts across four Tasreef phases, more than 36 km of planned new drainage lines with contracts expected complete by 2027, and an estimated AED 30 billion total program cost. Its 700% discharge-capacity increase is a long-term design target over the next 100 years, not an observed performance result.
value_dimensions: stormwater tunnel and network service; critical technology/logistics facilities; capital phasing and residual risk
validation_path: Acquire municipality project alignments, construction status, rainfall, and dated incident/road-closure records; stratify completed and under-construction assets before any exposure analysis.
scope_limit: Published capacity values are future program targets and cannot serve as observed flood truth or current system performance.

screening_rationale: India approved an urban flood risk mitigation program that includes Mumbai; city planning and IFLOWS document substantial flood research and warning needs.
value_integration_question: Test monsoon, coastal, drainage, and asset exposure; join satellite screening to the city’s flood-warning and mitigation evidence.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: India’s August 2026 UFRMP Phase I announcement includes Mumbai, with a city allocation of ₹707.71 crore and ₹150 crore reported released at that point. It documents funded implementation need; project completion and measured outcomes remain pending.
value_dimensions: drainage and flood-risk reduction; transport and public-service continuity; implementation equity across neighborhoods
validation_path: Use BMC/Maharashtra dated rainfall, drainage works, pump/gauge operations, and geocoded flood incident records; separately identify pre- and post-project dates and verify data translation and spatial resolution.
scope_limit: Approval and release establish program activity, not completed works, reduced flooding, or customer demand.

screening_rationale: World Bank city-region analysis documents interacting upstream runoff, intense local rainfall, and tidal effects.
value_integration_question: Test a deltaic megacity where river, pluvial, and tidal drivers overlap and require cross-system interpretation.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: World Bank urban-flood analysis describes Bangkok risk as the interaction of large upstream runoff, intense local rainfall, and tidal influence, with major flood-control works built following past floods. This makes the city a useful compound-driver comparator.
value_dimensions: urban drainage and river operations; commuter and utility access; upstream-to-city coordination
validation_path: Acquire Royal Irrigation Department and Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gauge, rainfall, pump, and event-closure records. Predefine local ground-truth sources and normalize Thai local time/date before matching satellite acquisitions.
scope_limit: The source is a planning/assessment report with historical context, not a current independent event label or an evaluation of ATLAS.

screening_rationale: World Bank work documents Tokyo-region urban flood risk management practice and the need to integrate risk into urban planning and investment.
value_integration_question: Test a mature infrastructure context and evaluate water-screening evidence alongside risk-informed planning and engineered controls.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: Tokyo Metropolitan Government reports that by October 2025 it had 30 operational storage basins across 14 rivers with about 2.73 million m³ capacity, plus about 12 km of diversion channels. It targets about 3.65 million m³ of total capacity by fiscal 2035 to address floods from rainfall above 50 mm/hour.
value_dimensions: storage and river-control infrastructure; dense transport and utility service; investment tracking
validation_path: Use Tokyo river/flood telemetry and rainfall with event reports and storage-facility service areas; assess source timestamps, datum and Japanese date/time conventions before event matching.
scope_limit: Capacity is metropolitan inventory/target, not proof of local flood absence or a satellite-classification accuracy measure.

screening_rationale: World Bank-supported Metro Manila Flood Management Project targets 17 cities/municipalities and more than one million people with pump/drainage upgrades.
value_integration_question: Test a high-need urban drainage and pumping portfolio with documented public investment and operations context.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
empirical_evidence: The World Bank describes the Metro Manila Flood Management Project as covering 17 cities/municipalities and targeting more than one million people through pumping-station, drainage, solid-waste and control-system improvements.
value_dimensions: pump-station service; drainage and solid-waste interactions; population and neighborhood access
validation_path: Obtain project pump and drainage locations, PAGASA rainfall, city/BWSC incident reports, and independently reviewed event extents. Resolve Metro Manila boundaries against the fixed city-center box and report only in-AOI evidence.
scope_limit: Project beneficiaries and footprint are regional targets, not actual affected persons or performance inside the candidate box.

screening_rationale: World Bank case material documents urban flood exposure, drainage constraints, and the need to combine structural and nonstructural measures.
value_integration_question: Test an inland megacity and connect observed-water evidence with drainage, land-use, and asset planning.
status: candidate; archive metadata screened; QA pixels and independent labels pending
need_evidence_type: municipal drainage plan and investment pipeline
empirical_evidence: São Paulo’s October 2026 drainage-plan release describes 201 interventions, 173 priority works, and a projected R$16.51 billion program through 2049. A separate municipal update reports 389 interventions completed since 2021; plan and commitment totals describe public management activity, not measured flood-loss reduction.
value_dimensions: stormwater works and maintenance; transport and community service; project priority and equity
validation_path: Join dated municipal flood incident and rainfall records to geocoded interventions; separate completed/active/planned works, and validate a held-out event against independently reviewed high-water or flood-extent data.
scope_limit: Municipal project totals are citywide, may span the candidate box unevenly, and are not measured reduction in risk or proof of ATLAS demand.
